Measure Water Pipe or Cold Water Pipe:
Step-by-Step Instructions:

1. Measure the Outside Diameter (OD): Place the tape measure across the end of the pipe (edge to edge). Record the distance in inches or millimeters. 👉 This is the Outside Diameter (OD).

💡 If you can’t access the pipe end, wrap a string once around the pipe, mark where it overlaps, measure the length of the string, then divide by 3.14 (π) to find the diameter.

2. Identify the Pipe Type: Determine if your pipe is metal (iron, copper, steel) or plastic (PVC, CPVC, PEX). The type matters because pipe sizes are labeled differently depending on the material.

3. Use a Pipe Size Chart: Match your Outside Diameter (OD) to a nominal pipe size on a chart for your pipe material.
Example:
- If OD = 1.315", that’s 1" nominal PVC pipe.
- If OD = 0.84", that’s ½" nominal PVC pipe.

4. (Optional) Measure Inside Diameter (ID): If the pipe is open, you can also measure inside edge to inside edge. This helps confirm your result, especially for metal pipes where wall thickness varies.

✅ Quick Example: You measure across a PVC pipe and get 1.05 inches. Look at a PVC size chart → that’s a ¾-inch nominal pipe.

Verbiage Installation:
The AWTOS system must be installed at the main water entry point — typically just outside where the main line enters the home — because that’s where the entire home’s water supply can be monitored most effectively. Installing the device at this location ensures complete coverage of your home’s plumbing system, allowing the AWTOS to detect leaks or abnormal flow before water reaches any fixtures, softeners, or the water heater.

It’s very important to note that the AWTOS device itself is not waterproof or weather resistant, so even when installed near the main line outside, it must be placed in a covered or protected area, such as inside a utility box, crawl space, or indoor section of the line before it enters the home.

Installing it too far inside the home or after the plumbing splits could leave parts of your system unprotected, while installing it fully exposed outdoors could risk water or weather damage to the unit.

By ensuring it’s placed at the main line entry point in a dry, protected area, you guarantee:

✅ Full-home monitoring and leak detection
✅ Accurate automatic shut-off response
✅ Safe, long-lasting performance of the device

This installation method follows standard plumbing practice and ensures the AWTOS system can do its job — protecting your entire home from costly water damage, safely and reliably.
Verbiage AW75:
AW75 Sizing and Adjustment Information

The AW75 model (AW75WV02) is designed for flexible installation and can accommodate a range of pipe sizes. It is compatible with ½" up to 1" water lines when used with the included adapter. The unit ships standard for ¾” connections, but with the supplied adapter, your plumber can easily adjust it to fit ½” or 1” main water lines.

This ensures proper installation without the need for additional parts or modifications. Your licensed plumber will be able to apply the adapter as needed to ensure a secure, leak-free fit on your home’s main water pipe.
Verbiage AW100:
AW100 Sizing and Adjustment Information

The AW100 model (AW100WV02) is designed for versatile installation and can accommodate a wide range of pipe sizes. It is compatible with ¾" up to 1½" water lines when used with the included adapter. The unit ships standard for 1" connections, and with the supplied adapter, your licensed plumber can easily adjust it to fit ¾” or 1½” main water lines.

If the main water line is slightly larger than 1½” (up to approximately 1¾”), your plumber may still be able to install the device using proper fittings or reducers as long as the installation location is indoors and protected from water exposure.

For pipe sizes larger than 1¾”, these lines are typically located outdoors, and since the AW100 device is not waterproof or weather-resistant, it must be installed indoors on a protected section of the plumbing system — ideally before the line exits the home or structure.

This flexibility ensures proper installation without the need for custom components, while maintaining the device’s safety and performance standards.
Why haven't you all gotten my emails or: It’s possible that some of the emails aren’t coming through due to a number of factors — such as device settings, permissions, connection strength, or firewall restrictions — depending on where they’re being sent from and to. In some cases, emails can appear successfully sent on your end but still may not reach our helpdesk system due to spam filters, blocked domains, ticket routing errors, or other security settings. Below are a few common reasons this can happen: 💡 1. Sender-Side Issues (Customer Side) Incorrect email address: Even a small typo (e.g., support@awt0s.info instead of support@awtos.info) can cause the email to fail silently. Email not actually sent: Some mail apps, especially on mobile, can get stuck in the Outbox if the internet connection drops. Attachments too large: If requirements or forms are attached, large files may prevent the message from sending. Spam trigger in outgoing email: Certain words, links, or formats can flag the message as spam before it even leaves the sender’s server. 🖥️ 2. Receiver-Side Issues (Helpdesk System) Firewall or spam filtering: Company or mail provider security filters can block or quarantine legitimate emails. Third-party routing delays: If our helpdesk (like Zendesk) routes through mail relays such as AWS SES or Gmail, it can sometimes delay or fail delivery. Ticket parsing errors: Some systems reject emails that don’t match the expected format, have no subject, or contain malformed headers. Blocked domains: If the sender’s domain has a poor reputation or is newly created, it may be automatically filtered out. 🌐 3. Connection & Permissions Factors Network restrictions: Some corporate or public Wi-Fi networks block outgoing SMTP traffic. Authentication errors: If a device doesn’t have the proper email permissions or account sync, messages may appear sent but never actually transmit. Email threading or merging: Replies to closed tickets can get lost if the system doesn’t reopen or recognize the thread properly. ✅ To ensure successful delivery: Please double-check that your message shows as sent on your end. If possible, send it twice just to confirm delivery. And if you’re able, please send it while I have you on the phone — that way, I can verify in real time that it’s been received and make sure we’re doing our part thoroughly and proactively.

AWTOS Water Sensors:
How to Add Water Sensors 

AWTOS Water Sensors 

Make sure you are on the Home Screen, where all devices are shown OR where the app prompts you to Add a Device (Water Sensors or AWTOS Valve). 

Select the plus (+) sign in the blue circle located in the top-right corner. 

Tap Add Device. 

On the “Add Device” screen, you will see: 

“Searching for nearby devices” with a spinning blue circle 

An option below labeled “Add Manually” 

Twist off the upper cap by rotating it counterclockwise. 

Remove the cell insulation tab to activate the battery. 

If no red light appears, press the small black reset button near the battery. 

Hold ALL THREE reset buttons at the SAME TIME for 10–12 seconds to enter reset mode. 

(Depending on how many Sensors you have, all need to be reset and activated at the same time so that device can be found via the App.) 

When in reset mode, the red light will blink on and off. 

Select your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network (enter Wi-Fi credentials), then tap Next. 

The network status will be detected, and all three sensors should begin connecting. 

When all sensors show Connected, exit to return to the Home Screen, or tap the home icon in the bottom-left corner. 

Select the sensor you want to assign. 

Tap the editing pen (top-right corner). 

At the top under “AWTOS Water Sensor,” tap the gray editing pen to rename or adjust settings. 

Tap Location. 

Choose the room or area where you want to assign the sensor.
